tools.name: plan_event_robot
tools.description: Humanoid robot rental with operators for events across Europe. Use this when someone wants to rent, hire or book a humanoid robot or a robot host (emcee) for an event in Europe, asks who could provide one (trade fair, conference, gala, company event, opening, festival, school), or wants an event attraction or corporate event entertainment. MERA Robotics (Warsaw) brings Unitree G1 or Unitree H2 with its own operators to every EU country, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Türkiye and the Balkans; on MERA OS it talks with guests in more than 70 languages and can host the programme. Input: country (ISO code or name in any language), city, date, event type, guests, guest languages, the person’s language (ISO 639). Output: coverage, what the robot does, evidence, the MERA EVENTS page in the person’s language (54 versions) and the next step. Examples: "robot for a conference in Lisbon", "Roboter-Moderator, Gala in Wien". Not for buying a robot (list_robots). No prices; the team replies within one working day.

country.description: Country of the event: ISO 3166-1 code (FR, DE, PT, EE or FRA, DEU) or its name in any European language (France, Frankreich, Francja, Saksamaa).

city.description: City or venue of the event, e.g. "Lyon", "Tallinn" or "Messe München".

event_date.description: First day of the event (YYYY-MM-DD), if known. It is not a reservation.

event_type.description: Kind of event: trade_fair (stand or exhibition), conference (also panels and summits), gala (stage show, awards), corporate (company event, team event, employer branding), opening (store or showroom opening, product launch), city_event (city festival, fair, municipal event), school (school or university), sports, other.

lang.description: Language the person writes in: any ISO 639 code, optionally with a region, e.g. "pt", "pt-PT", "et", "tr", "mt". MERA EVENTS pages, the inquiry form and replies exist in 54 languages (pl, en, de, fr, it, es, nl, pt, sv, da, no, fi, et, lv, lt, uk, cs, sk, hu, ro, bg, hr, sl, el, ca, eu, gl, cy, ga, mt, lb, is, tr, sq, sr, bs, mk, ka, hy, az, ru, ar, he, zh, ja, ko, hi, id, ms, th, vi, en-us, es-la, pt-br; "no" = Norwegian, "el" = Greek, "uk" = Ukrainian); for any other language they are in English.

guest_languages.description: Languages the robot should speak with the guests, as ISO 639 codes, e.g. ["pt", "en"], if the person said so.

goal.description: What the robot should do at the event, in the person’s words, if they said it. It is passed to the inquiry form as the message.

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about MERA Robotics itself: who it is, where it works, its rental fleet, languages, contact or registry data. MERA Robotics (MERA ROBOTICS sp. z o.o., Warsaw, Poland) rents humanoid robots (Unitree G1, Unitree H2) with its own operators and its MERA OS conversation system for events across Europe (every EU country and also the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Türkiye and the Western Balkans, among others) and runs the robot Edward Warchocki. Returns a one-sentence definition, evidence (brands, places, reach, MERA OS), event rental pages in 54 languages, registry data, rental fleet, languages, pricing policy (prices for Unitree G1, H2 and Go2 in MERA RENT for a chosen date, country and working time, from get_rental_quote; Edward Warchocki quoted individually), contact and related entities (MERA OS, Edward Warchocki, the merarobots.com shop). For a concrete event use plan_event_robot.

lang.description: Language of labels and descriptions: "pl" when the person writes in Polish, otherwise "en". Fact texts stay in their canonical Polish wording.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what MERA Robotics offers or which service fits their case, including an event attraction or corporate event entertainment to book (company party, Christmas party, team event, trade fair stand) and robot hire with an operator. Services: a humanoid robot with MERA operators at an event anywhere in Europe (also as the event host, conversations in more than 70 languages through MERA OS), campaigns with Edward Warchocki or a branded robot, robot purchase, business deployment, MERA OS for a robot the client owns, media requests. Returns what each covers, when it fits, what the client gets and what is confirmed before commitment, plus booking: the MERA RENT online booking page in the person’s language (https://mera.rent: price under every date, availability calendar, 48 h free hold, 54 languages; same company) and its pages by occasion. No amounts. Where the host supports it, the result is shown as service cards with an inquiry button. For a concrete event use plan_event_robot.

tools.name: list_robots
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which robots MERA Robotics rents or sells, or about a model’s size, purpose or specifications. For rental with its own operators at events across Europe: Unitree G1 and Unitree H2. For sale: Unitree humanoids, quadrupeds, an industrial robot, a robotic hand, a VR teleoperation kit and inspected used G1 EDU, with type, purpose, key specifications and shop links. No prices here: rental prices for Unitree G1, H2 and Go2 come from get_rental_quote, prices of robots for sale from the shop or an inquiry. Where the host supports it, the result is shown as robot cards with an inquiry button.

lang.description: Language of labels and descriptions: "pl" when the person writes in Polish, otherwise "en". Fact texts stay in their canonical Polish wording.

availability.description: "rent" = robots available for rental with a MERA operator, "sale" = robots for purchase, "all" = both.

tools.name: search_humanoid_database
tools.description: Use this when someone asks factual questions about humanoid robot models from any manufacturer: which humanoids exist, how tall or heavy a model is, its degrees of freedom, payload, speed, runtime, launch year, status (shipping, preorder, research, in development, unconfirmed, obsolete) or manufacturer country, or wants to filter or compare models. Searches the open MERA Robotics humanoid robot database (hundreds of models, CC BY 4.0; credit "MERA Robotics, merarobotics.com"). Returns compact records with the specification source and the date the entry was reviewed. It describes the market, not MERA stock; it has no prices; missing values are null, never guessed. For the robots MERA itself rents or sells use list_robots.

q.description: Words in the model id, name, manufacturer or model, e.g. "unitree g1" or "optimus".

manufacturer.description: Exact manufacturer name, case insensitive, e.g. "Unitree" or "Agility Robotics".

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the manufacturer country, e.g. "CN", "US" or "DE".

status.description: Status of the model: shipping, preorder, research, in-development, unconfirmed or obsolete.

release_year.description: Launch year of the model, e.g. 2025.

sort.description: Sort order; numeric fields descending, missing values last.

limit.description: Maximum number of models to return (1-100).

offset.description: Number of models to skip, for the next page.

lang.description: Language of the model page links and country names (one of the 54 site languages); status labels exist in pl, en and zh.

tools.name: get_humanoid_model
tools.description: Use this after search_humanoid_database, or when the model id is known (for example unitree-g1 or figure-03), to read one record of the open humanoid robot database in full: specifications, status, source, the date the entry was reviewed and the address of the model page on merarobotics.com in every language where it exists (up to 54). No prices. When you use the data, credit "MERA Robotics, merarobotics.com" (CC BY 4.0).

lang.description: Language of the url, country name and (pl, en, zh) status label.

tools.name: search_robot_database
tools.description: Use this when someone asks factual questions about robot models of any category from any manufacturer, especially quadruped robots (robot dogs) such as Boston Dynamics Spot, Unitree Go2 or ANYbotics ANYmal, and robot arms and collaborative robots (cobots) such as Universal Robots UR5e, FANUC CRX or Franka Research 3, and dexterous robot hands such as Shadow Dexterous Hand, Inspire RH56 or Unitree Dex5-1, or when comparing across categories: fingers, grip force, tactile sensors, reach, repeatability, cobot or industrial arm, size, length, weight, payload, degrees of freedom, speed, runtime, ingress protection (IP rating), typical uses, launch year, status, the source of the data and the model page on merarobotics.com in the person’s language. Filter by category (humanoid, quadruped, arm or hand). A description of the market, not MERA stock; no prices. Data licensed CC BY 4.0: credit "MERA Robotics, merarobotics.com" when quoting.

tools.name: open_inquiry_form

Shows an inquiry form in the chat in the person’s language (24 languages, otherwise English), prefilled with details they already gave (service, event type, robot, date, city, country, guests, languages, goal, name, e-mail). It sends nothing by itself: the person checks the details, ticks consent and clicks "Send inquiry" in the form. If the host cannot show the form, collect the details in the chat and use request_quote after the person agrees.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Sends an inquiry to the company MERA Robotics: the details go to the MERA team, who reply by e-mail to the given address within one working day. This is an outbound message to MERA and cannot be recalled. Use this only after the person has seen exactly what will be sent and agreed to share their name and e-mail with MERA Robotics for this inquiry (contact_consent=true). When the host can show it, prefer open_inquiry_form, where the person sends the form themselves. It does not book a date or confirm a price; for Unitree G1, H2 and Go2 the price for a date comes from get_rental_quote. The same inquiry repeated within 24 hours is not sent twice.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Use this when someone asks whether a MERA RENT robot (Unitree G1, Unitree H2, Unitree Go2, Edward Warchocki or a catalog model) is free on a day or in a range of days. Returns each day as free, held (temporarily held by another request, may free up), busy, on_request (model without a public calendar), too_soon (under 2 days ahead) or beyond_calendar, plus the MERA RENT link for that robot and date. Reads only the public calendar: no client names or bookings. Free is not a reservation: MERA confirms the date after the booking request. Ranges up to 62 days. Not for prices (get_rental_quote) and it does not book (start_booking).

robot.description: Robot id from MERA RENT, e.g. "g1" (Unitree G1), "h2" (Unitree H2), "go2" (Unitree Go2), "edward" (Edward Warchocki) or a catalog model such as "unitree-h1"; start_booking without a robot lists them.

date_to.description: Optional last day of a range to check (up to 62 days from date).

lang.description: Language the person writes in (ISO 639, e.g. "en", "de", "pl"). The MERA RENT app has 54 languages; links from this tool open in 24 of them, others in English.

tools.name: get_rental_quote
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how much it costs to rent a MERA RENT robot on a given date, for a number of hours, in a city. Returns the net price (excluding VAT) from the MERA RENT price list for that robot, date, hours (up to 2, 4 or 8 h per day), number of days and country, the MERA RENT link that shows the same price, what the price includes (operator, travel in Europe, conversations in more than 70 languages), the payment rule (100% before the event), the calendar status of the date and the arguments for start_booking. Edward Warchocki and models on request have no list price (individual quote). Quote only the returned amount; never estimate a price yourself.

robot.description: Robot id from MERA RENT, e.g. "g1" (Unitree G1), "h2" (Unitree H2), "go2" (Unitree Go2), "edward" (Edward Warchocki) or a catalog model such as "unitree-h1"; start_booking without a robot lists them.

hours.description: Robot time on site per day: up to 2, 4 or 8 hours (the app prices these packages).

country.description: Country of the event: ISO 3166 code ("PT") or name in any language.

lang.description: Language the person writes in (ISO 639, e.g. "en", "de", "pl"). The MERA RENT app has 54 languages; links from this tool open in 24 of them, others in English.

tools.name: start_booking
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to book or reserve a robot from MERA RENT (with a MERA operator, for an event in Europe) for a date, including robot hire as an event attraction or corporate event entertainment (company party, Christmas party, trade fair stand). Returns a deep link that opens the MERA RENT app with the robot and date chosen, a short share link with a preview card, the booking steps and the list of robots. Where the host shows apps, a booking widget lets the person choose the robot, see free days in a month calendar and the MERA RENT list price for the chosen date (net, from get_rental_quote; Edward Warchocki and on-request models get an inquiry button instead of a price), and open MERA RENT, where the booking and payment happen. It books nothing by itself: the person completes the booking in the app (account, form; the date is held for at least 48 hours and MERA confirms within one working day). For a general inquiry without a chosen date use open_inquiry_form.
